name: llhttp
baseline: http_parser (nodejs/http-parser, the parser llhttp replaced in Node.js)
workload: HTTP request parsing benchmark over 8192 mb of input, reporting bandwidth, requests per second and wall time for llhttp (C output) versus http_parser; request mix is not stated in the README.
claimed_speedup: README table: llhttp 1777.24 mb/s, 3583799.39 req/sec, 4.61 s versus http_parser 694.66 mb/s, 1406180.33 req/sec, 11.79 s on 8192.00 mb of input; 'llhttp is faster by approximately 156%' (about 2.56x bandwidth, derived from page data).
stars_or_usage: 1.9k stars; the HTTP/1 parser in Node.js
tradeoffs: Parser is generated from a TypeScript state-machine description by llparse and shipped as C (llhttp.c plus about 450 lines of C helpers); ABI/API differs from http_parser (callbacks and llhttp_t instead of http_parser_settings); strict and lenient flag modes exist.
caveats: First-party README numbers only: the table states no CPU, compiler, flags or request mix and is undated (the same table is already in the v2.0.0 README). The repo's current bench/native.ts and bench/wasm.ts time llhttp only; the http_parser side that produced the table is not in the current tree, so the numbers cannot be reproduced from public code. Makefile builds the library with clang -Os -g3, so benchmark flags are unknown. Mixed units in the table (mb versus req) are as printed. No independent shootout was found in reachable sources (blogs and the Node.js post are egress-blocked).
found_via: seed-record pass: awesome-c (oz123) Networking-and-Internet 'HTTP request/response parser', then https://github.com/nodejs/llhttp README

name: LibTorrent (rakshasa)
baseline: official BitTorrent client (the original mainline client; not named more exactly in the claim)
workload: Seeding speed on high-bandwidth connections; no further workload description.
claimed_speedup: 'On high-bandwidth connections it is able to seed at 3 times the speed of the official client.' (old project description repeated in distro package texts; snippet only)
stars_or_usage: 1k stars; the engine of the rTorrent client
tradeoffs: C++ for *nix only (epoll and select polling); transfers directly from file pages (mmap) to the network stack; GPL with an OpenSSL linking exception, sha_fast code triple-licensed MPL/LGPL/GPL; API is built for rTorrent and uses sigc++ signals in older releases.
caveats: Snippet only: the 3x sentence was surfaced by WebSearch from SlackBuilds and other distro package descriptions; those hosts were egress-blocked for WebFetch, so the page was not opened. The sentence is not in the current README, the wiki home page, or the v0.13.6 README (checked). Baseline 'official client' is vague (the original Python BitTorrent client of roughly 2005-2008), with no methodology, hardware, torrent size, peer count or version, so the claim is old, first-party and unreproducible. Current README says only 'high performance' without numbers.
found_via: seed-record pass: awesome-cpp (fffaraz) 'BitTorrent library' entry, then github.com/rakshasa/libtorrent and a WebSearch for its performance claim
